sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 1! On the left, explore an 8-node provenance DAG. Toggle any upstream node to watch the blast radius cascade. On the right, tune the distribution shift sliders to observe 1D Wasserstein Earth Mover's distance and generalization error bounds.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, let's stress test the lineage DAG! Notice how corrupting raw feature node V2 instantly invalidates the embedding store and downstream models, while the Wasserstein shift canvas reveals rising generalization risk!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1! A clinical diagnostic model has training loss 0.06 with Lipschitz constant 1.5. On a new hospital cohort, sensor drift gives Wasserstein distance 0.12 with domain discrepancy 0.04. Calculate the evaluation loss upper bound and evaluate safety at threshold 0.35.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1! Let's solve: training loss 0.06, Lipschitz factor 1.5, Wasserstein distance 0.12, and discrepancy 0.04. Calculate the theoretical error bound. Can this model be certified safe without fine-tuning?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding derivation! Option B is correct. Two times Lipschitz constant 1.5 times Wasserstein distance 0.12 equals 0.36. Adding training loss 0.06 and discrepancy 0.04 yields an upper bound of 0.46. Because 0.46 exceeds the safety threshold of 0.35, deployment must be blocked pending domain adaptation!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Option B is correct. Recall the Wasserstein generalization bound: evaluation loss is bounded by training loss plus two times Lipschitz constant times Wasserstein distance plus domain discrepancy. Substituting the parameters yields 0.46, which breaches the safety threshold of 0.35!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 2! Inspect the MinHash LSH signature collision matrix across hash permutations k from 64 to 2048, and explore the benchmark contamination mixture model to observe how memorization inflates observed accuracy.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, look at the decontamination curve! When contamination fraction is 25% with 100% memorization, an observed score of 86% drops to a true generalizable accuracy of only 81.33%! Benchmark leakage completely distorts the leaderboard!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2! An open-source model reports 86.0% observed accuracy on a benchmark with 25% verbatim contamination and 100% memorized accuracy. Calculate the true generalizable accuracy, and find the minimum MinHash permutations k needed for epsilon 0.04 at 95% confidence.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2 challenge! Observed score 86%, contamination rate 25%, and memorization rate 100%. What is the true de-biased score, and how many MinHash hash functions k are required?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! Option A is correct. Under the mixture model, true accuracy equals 0.86 minus 0.25 divided by 0.75, which yields exactly 81.33%. By the Chernoff bound, k must be at least natural log of 40 divided by two times 0.04 squared, which equals 1,153 hash permutations!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: That's not right. Option A is correct. True accuracy is recovered by the de-biasing formula yielding 81.33%. For MinHash sample sizing, the Chernoff bound requires k greater than or equal to ln of two over delta divided by two epsilon squared, giving 1,153 hash functions.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 3! In an 8-node enterprise lineage DAG, a corrupt sensor calibration enters at feature node V2, directly and indirectly feeding 5 downstream nodes. What is the blast radius contamination fraction, and how is it remediated under content-addressed storage?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Final checkpoint! Corrupted data enters at node V2 in an 8-node DAG, contaminating 5 downstream vertices. What is the blast radius fraction, and what is the surgical remediation under cryptographic CAS?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Masterclass comprehension! Option C is correct. The blast radius includes 5 downstream nodes plus V2 itself (6 nodes out of 8, or 75.0% contamination fraction). Under cryptographic content-addressed storage, we surgically invalidate only the affected branch hashes without wiping uncorrupted historical partitions!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Option C is correct. The forward reachability cone includes node V2 and all 5 dependent vertices, giving 6 out of 8 nodes or 75.0% contamination. Content-addressed storage allows surgical invalidation of the affected hash branch without re-running uncorrupted DAG stages.
